reference_findings.diagnosis: MINOCA is a working description after MI criteria with non-obstructive coronary arteries; it is not a final mechanism diagnosis. Further evaluation is needed to distinguish plaque disruption, spasm, embolism, myocarditis, Takotsubo and other causes.
reference_findings.risk_assessment: High concern / mechanism unresolved; qualitative simulation label only, not a validated score.

investigation_reports.ecg: Transient ST-T changes; no persistent STEMI pattern in the available tracing.
investigation_reports.laboratory_panel: Serial hs-cTn shows a clear rise/fall above fictional assay threshold; CBC and renal function without major simulated abnormality.
investigation_reports.echocardiography: LVEF 53%; subtle inferolateral hypokinesis; no effusion.
investigation_reports.coronary_or_other_imaging: Reference coronary angiography: no stenosis >=50%; mild irregularities only; TIMI 3 flow. No OCT/IVUS or cardiac MRI result at entry.
investigation_reports.initial_vitals: HR 86 bpm; BP 126/78 mmHg; RR 18/min; SpO2 98%; stable.
investigation_reports.not_supplied: Any test not explicitly listed is not ordered/not available; it must not be interpreted as normal.

history.chief_complaint: Acute chest pain with troponin rise and ischemic ECG changes.
history.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began at rest; initial work-up supports myocardial injury, but coronary angiography shows no obstructive lesion.
relevant_history: Recent viral-like illness is included as a possible clue but is not diagnostic

differential_diagnosis: Plaque disruption not apparent on angiography

pathway_review.label: Continue structured mechanism-focused evaluation, including cardiac MRI and coronary assessment as clinically appropriate
pathway_review.reason: MINOCA is a working diagnosis; mechanism determines subsequent management.

pathway_review.label: Stop after writing “MINOCA” as the final cause
pathway_review.reason: Confuses a working diagnosis with the underlying mechanism.

pathway_review.reason: Mechanisms differ; the case should teach cause-based reasoning.

reference_findings.safety_review: Review contrast/renal status before additional imaging, check medication and allergy history, monitor for recurrent symptoms and ensure the learner distinguishes myocardial injury from confirmed mechanism.
reference_findings.simulated_clinical_course: Reference branch: cardiac MRI suggests a non-ischemic myocarditis pattern in the hidden answer; learner is graded on keeping the differential open and ordering suitable clarification, not guessing early.
learning_objectives: MINOCA is not a final etiologic diagnosis.
Use cardiac MRI and additional tests selectively to resolve mechanism.
reference_findings.review_note: Synthetic scenario. Clinical values and pathway labels require qualified interventional cardiology review before deployment. Educational use only; not real-patient guidance.
